text:
alex: Heads up — seeing slow mem growth on kv-3 during the long-context perf harness. Not a leak per-se, looks like KV cache fragment accumulation (many <256B holes) after ~30m of steady traffic. Attaching the tiny histogram snapshot and a short heap log we captured.

maya: Ugh. Can you paste the allocation histogram?

alex: ```
kv_alloc_hist: {
  size_bins: [64,128,256,512,1024,2048],
  counts: [1423, 987, 312, 43, 12, 3],
  free_bins: [1200, 900, 290, 33, 9, 1]  # note heavy population in 64/128 with mismatched free counts
}
heap_log_tail: 
[2025-06-12T14:01:02Z] live_kv_blocks=678432 total_alloc_bytes=2.1GB kv_cache_bytes=1.9GB
[2025-06-12T14:05:02Z] live_kv_blocks=679120 total_alloc_bytes=2.12GB kv_cache_bytes=1.92GB
[2025-06-12T14:10:02Z] live_kv_blocks=679980 total_alloc_bytes=2.14GB kv_cache_bytes=1.94GB
```

sam: Interesting — lots of tiny blocks in use, but free bins still high? Could be internal fragmentation: allocator hands out 256B slices but workloads use 40–200B variable keys so remainder becomes unusable due to slabization.

ina: Is this the buddy allocator or the new slab-sliced allocator option? We rolled slab-sliced on kv-3 last week.

alex: slab-sliced. We enabled it to reduce large-block waste. Looks like side-effect is many micro-slices that don't get coalesced when adjacent slots free at different times.

ryan: Could be allocation hysteresis: allocator avoids immediate coalesce to avoid churn, but over long contexts that leaves persistent microholes. We saw similar in redis when eviction heuristics are gentle.

alloc-bot: profiler:kv-3: kv_cache_fragmentation_ratio=0.18 kv_cache_reuse_hitrate=0.73 avg_free_run_length=3.2 compaction_ops_last_hour=4

maya: 0.18 frag ratio is non-trivial at our scale. Reuse hitrate 0.73 could be improved. Any pattern by sequence length?

alex: Yes — traces show long-context requests create long KV chains but tail requests are short and write back smaller kv entries, leaving gaps at the tail of slices. Sequence-based allocation seems to favor LIFO and leaves older neighboring slices untouched.

sam: Ideas: 1) Add deferred merging pass during low-load windows (e.g., compaction window every 5m) 2) Tune slice size distribution: add 192B bin to better match median small write 3) Opportunistic remap: when block reuse fails X times, try relocate to compact.

ina: 1 and 2 look low-risk. 3 might be expensive (copying KV entries). But we can add heuristics: only relocate if we save >= 3 slices or ratio > threshold.

alex: I ran a quick sim: adding 192B bin reduced fragmentation ratio to ~0.11 in sim with same trace. Deferred compaction (5m window, budget 2% cpu) further dropped to 0.07. Relocation gave best but at 12% CPU overhead in sim.

maya: Nice. Can you share sim config? Would like to reproduce locally.

alex: ```
SIM_CFG:
  slab_mode: slab-sliced
  slice_bins: [64,128,192,256,512]
  compaction: {window_secs: 300, budget_cpu_pct: 2, min_merge_gain: 2}  # min gain is slices reclaimed
  relocation: {enabled:false, max_copy_bytes:65536, min_gain:4}
```

ryan: For production, prefer a staged rollout: enable 192 bin on a canary host, watch frag ratio and latency p99. Compaction should be throttled — we already saw background compaction affect tail-latency if unbounded.

sam: Agree. Also consider changing allocation policy to prefer first-fit with occasional best-fit sampling to avoid creating many small leftover fragments. First-fit is fast but creates fragmentation patterns; randomized best-fit can reduce leftovers at modest CPU cost.

alex: Noted. I'm going to open a small PR that: 1) adds 192B bin + config flag, 2) implements compaction scheduling with budget, 3) exposes allocator metrics (avg_free_run_length, holes_count_by_bin) via console.

maya: please include a toggle to turn relocation on per-host. We'll need metrics to evaluate CPU tradeoff.

ryan: Also add a perf test that replays long-context traces for 1h and records frag ratio + tail latency. QA should run this as part of the canary.

alex: Will do. Quick question: should compaction try to compact across different slabs or only within slab-class? Cross-slab compaction would be heavier.

sam: Keep it intra-slab initially. Cross-slab may require pointer remapping in the route table — risky. If intra-slab fails to reach threshold, consider compaction + slab-eviction (move active entries to new slab then free entire slab).

ina: Also add a safeguard: if last compaction increased p99 by >10% within 5m, back off auto-compaction for 15m.

alex: Good call. I'll prototype and post numbers. Planning canary tomorrow on kv-canary-2 with 192 bin and compaction budget=2%.

maya: :thumbsup: Keep us posted. If canary looks good we can roll to the rest of slab-sliced fleet next week.

alloc-bot: deploy-notice: canary-bundle queued on kv-canary-2 (bundle id: b-20250612-03)

alex: Thanks all — I'll paste the PR and sim logs once ready.
